genxml.title: Bedrock processor interface (PI) registers: field layouts, interrupt banks, real-time clock, graphics credits and error capture
genxml.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
genxml.doc: Offsets are hub-relative inside one processor interface. The second interface repeats the same layout 2 MiB higher in the node window (see the processor-interface page). Register names, offsets, widths and field positions come from the public Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header, so they are established as header facts. Behaviour the header gives only in its comments is inferred. Access modes the header does not state are assumed read and write and labelled so in the text. The header gives no reset value for any register, so every reset is unknown.

struct.name: CPU_PROTECT
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: One bit per region. A set bit lets the processor in that region reach this interface's local registers. A denied access gets a protection error reply. The header says the register is not reset by a soft reset and gives no reset value.

struct.name: PROT_OVERRIDE
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: A write carrying a special data pattern sets the writing processor's region bit in the CPU protect register. The header does not give the pattern.

struct.name: IO_PROTECT
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: One bit per region. Decides whether I/O-initiated interrupt writes from that region may set bits in the two pending banks. The header says it is not reset by a soft reset.

struct.name: REGION_PRESENT
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: One bit per region. Clear bits block speculative coherent reads to that region. A coherent read to an absent region gets an error reply and no error register changes. Partial reads and writes are not checked. Cached-alias accesses are not affected. The header says it is not reset by a soft reset.

struct.name: CPU_NUM
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Read by a processor to learn its own slot and interface. Bit 0 is the slot (0 for CPU A, 1 for CPU B); bit 1 is the interface (0 for PI0, 1 for PI1).

struct.name: CALIAS_SIZE
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Size code for the cached-alias space. The header says all cached-alias spaces in a system must carry the same size. It is not reset by a soft reset.

struct.name: MAX_CRB_TIMEOUT
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Value at which a valid coherency request buffer's timeout counter causes a timeout error. The header refers to the processor interface chapter of the Bedrock manual, which is not held.

struct.name: CRB_SCALE_FACTOR
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Sets how often a valid coherency request buffer's timeout counter increments. The header refers to the same manual section as the maximum timeout register.

struct.name: CPU_PRESENT_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Set by the interface when it sees the first transaction from CPU A. The header gives no write behaviour.

struct.name: CPU_PRESENT_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Set by the interface when it sees the first transaction from CPU B. The header gives no write behaviour.

struct.name: CPU_ENABLE_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: While clear, the interface ignores the bus request from CPU A and never grants it the bus. The header says it is not reset by a soft reset and gives no reset value.

struct.name: CPU_ENABLE_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: While clear, the interface ignores the bus request from CPU B and never grants it the bus. The header says it is not reset by a soft reset and gives no reset value.

struct.name: NMI_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: A write issues a non-maskable interrupt to CPU A. The header gives no predicate on the written value, no latch behaviour and no reset value.

struct.name: NMI_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: A write issues a non-maskable interrupt to CPU B. The header gives no predicate on the written value, no latch behaviour and no reset value.

struct.name: IPI_A
struct.doc: Inter-processor interrupt delivery for the Itanium processor in slot A of this interface (IA-64 nodes only). A store of (delivery mode << 8) | vector, 64 bits wide, raises that vector on the processor. The Linux code stores to this offset of PI0 for slice 0 and PI1 for slice 2, from the node's hub register window. The MIPS headers do not define the offset and no MIPS software is known to use it. The register's reset, read behaviour and any mode beyond the written value are unknown.

struct.name: IPI_B
struct.doc: Inter-processor interrupt delivery for the Itanium processor in slot B of this interface (IA-64 nodes only), same use as ipi_a: slice 1 on PI0, slice 3 on PI1.

struct.name: INT_PEND_MOD
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Sets or clears one bit of an interrupt pending bank. It is the only pending-register write an I/O-issued write may make, and I/O protect checks it. Processor writes are checked against CPU protect. The header gives no reset value.

struct.name: INT_PEND0
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Pending bank 0, read only. The bits map to interrupt level 2 in the header's naming. The graphics bits are set by hardware and must be cleared by software.

struct.name: INT_PEND1
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Pending bank 1, read only. Bits map to interrupt level 3 unless the remap register moves bits 31 to 0 to level 2. The correctable-error, NACK and performance-overflow bits are set by hardware and must be cleared by software. The system shutdown, network, local-block and crossbar bits only reflect other logic and cannot be changed through this interface.

struct.name: INT_MASK0_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Masks bank 0 for CPU A. A set bit passes the pending bit through as a level 2 interrupt (bit 10 of the processor's Cause register).

struct.name: INT_MASK1_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Masks bank 1 for CPU A. Bits 63 to 32 always raise a level 3 interrupt (bit 11 of Cause). Bits 31 to 0 raise level 3 or level 2 depending on the remap register. The header says only one processor per Bedrock should enable the network, local-block, crossbar and memory-correctable bits.

struct.name: INT_MASK0_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Masks bank 0 for CPU B. Same layout and meaning as the CPU A mask.

struct.name: INT_MASK1_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Masks bank 1 for CPU B. Same layout and meaning as the CPU A mask.

struct.name: CC_PEND_SET_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: A store by a CPU sets the bit for the storing processor's region in the CPU A CPU-to-CPU pending register. These registers have no access protection.

struct.name: CC_PEND_SET_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: A store by a CPU sets the bit for the storing processor's region in the CPU B CPU-to-CPU pending register. These registers have no access protection.

struct.name: CC_PEND_CLR_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: A read returns the CPU A CPU-to-CPU pending bits. A write clears each bit whose data bit is one.

struct.name: CC_PEND_CLR_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: A read returns the CPU B CPU-to-CPU pending bits. A write clears each bit whose data bit is one.

struct.name: CC_MASK
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Masks both CPU-to-CPU pending registers.

struct.name: INT_PEND1_REMAP
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Moves bank 1 bits 31 to 0 from level 3 to level 2 under control of the low four bits. Bit 4 forwards the memory and unit error interrupts to the I/O interface, which raises its interrupt to the node named in its destination register, so the errors can reach another node. The header does not give the encoding of the four-bit selector.

struct.name: RT_COMPARE_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: When the real-time counter equals this value, the CPU A real-time pending bit is set. The header's comment says this sends a level 4 interrupt. Access is not stated; read and write is assumed.

struct.name: RT_COMPARE_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: When the real-time counter equals this value, the CPU B real-time pending bit is set. The header's comment says this sends a level 4 interrupt. Access is not stated; read and write is assumed.

struct.name: PROFILE_COMPARE
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: When the low 32 bits of the real-time counter equal this value, both profiling pending registers are set to one. Access is not stated; read and write is assumed.

struct.name: RT_INT_PEND_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Real-time interrupt pending for CPU A. When the matching enable is set, CPU A's interrupt line follows this bit. The header's comment on this register says level 5, which conflicts with the compare register's level 4. Any store clears the bit.

struct.name: RT_INT_PEND_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Real-time interrupt pending for CPU B. When the matching enable is set, CPU B's interrupt line follows this bit. The header's comment says level 5. Any store clears the bit.

struct.name: PROF_INT_PEND_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Profiling interrupt pending for CPU A. Set when the profile compare matches. Any store clears it. The A and B copies are separate so each can be cleared alone.

struct.name: PROF_INT_PEND_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Profiling interrupt pending for CPU B. Set when the profile compare matches. Any store clears it.

struct.name: RT_INT_EN_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Enables the real-time interrupt to CPU A.

struct.name: RT_INT_EN_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Enables the real-time interrupt to CPU B.

struct.name: PROF_INT_EN_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Enables the profiling interrupt to CPU A.

struct.name: PROF_INT_EN_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Enables the profiling interrupt to CPU B.

struct.name: DEBUG_SEL
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Selects the debug data the interface drives, together with the debug module's select. The header gives the selector names below and says the B-select bit chooses CPU A or CPU B logic for some selections. Each low and high selector bit is one signal, named by the header as follows: low selector bits are t5cc A, t5cc B, totcc A, totcc B, reqcc A, reqcc B, rplcc A, rplcc B, intcc, perf increment A 0 and 1, perf increment B 0 and 1; high selector bits are the same names in the same order.

struct.name: INT_PEND_MOD_ALIAS
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Alias of the pending-modify register with the same layout and checks. The header does not say why a second address exists.

struct.name: GFX_PAGE_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Graphics page for CPU A. Uncached I/O stores into the enabled page are graphics write commands tracked by the credit counter, not ordinary write commands. Access is not stated; read and write is assumed.

struct.name: GFX_CREDIT_CNTR_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Graphics credit counter for CPU A. It drops by one per doubleword sent to graphics and rises by one per doubleword acknowledged. When it is below the bias, the header says write-ready is withheld, an interrupt is sent, and write-ready is allowed again. Access is not stated; read and write is assumed.

struct.name: GFX_BIAS_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Graphics bias for CPU A. When the credit counter is at or below this value, the header says a flow-control interrupt is sent. Access is not stated; read and write is assumed.

struct.name: GFX_INT_CNTR_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Graphics interrupt counter for CPU A. The header says it is written by software, loaded from the compare on an interrupt, NMI or soft reset, zeroed when the credit counter rises above the bias, and counts one per clock while the credit counter is at or below zero. Access is not stated; read and write is assumed.

struct.name: GFX_INT_CMP_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Graphics interrupt compare for CPU A. The interrupt is sent when the interrupt counter reaches this value. Access is not stated; read and write is assumed.

struct.name: GFX_PAGE_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Graphics page for CPU B. Uncached I/O stores into the enabled page are graphics write commands tracked by the credit counter, not ordinary write commands. Access is not stated; read and write is assumed.

struct.name: GFX_CREDIT_CNTR_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Graphics credit counter for CPU B. It drops by one per doubleword sent to graphics and rises by one per doubleword acknowledged. When it is below the bias, the header says write-ready is withheld, an interrupt is sent, and write-ready is allowed again. Access is not stated; read and write is assumed.

struct.name: GFX_BIAS_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Graphics bias for CPU B. When the credit counter is at or below this value, the header says a flow-control interrupt is sent. Access is not stated; read and write is assumed.

struct.name: GFX_INT_CNTR_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Graphics interrupt counter for CPU B. The header says it is written by software, loaded from the compare on an interrupt, NMI or soft reset, zeroed when the credit counter rises above the bias, and counts one per clock while the credit counter is at or below zero. Access is not stated; read and write is assumed.

struct.name: GFX_INT_CMP_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Graphics interrupt compare for CPU B. The interrupt is sent when the interrupt counter reaches this value. Access is not stated; read and write is assumed.

struct.name: ERR_INT_PEND_WR
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Writable view of the error interrupt pending bits. A read returns every error source. A direct write sets or clears each unreserved bit, except the memory uncorrectable bit. Bit layout is the same as the write-with-clear register.

struct.name: ERR_INT_PEND
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Error interrupt pending. A read returns every error source. A store clears each bit whose data bit is one. Bits 0 to 23 are twelve CPU B and CPU A pairs with B at the even bit, in order: spool complete, spurious message, the two write-buffer error kinds, system-state parity, system data ECC, system address ECC, command data parity, command address parity, spool error, uncached uncorrectable, system-state tag. Bit 24 is memory uncorrectable. Bits 25 to 34 are five pairs with A at the even bit: bad data, cached uncorrectable, packet length, request-buffer error and request-buffer timeout.

struct.name: ERR_INT_MASK_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Masks the error pending bits for CPU A. A set bit lets that error raise the level 6 interrupt to CPU A. The header says only one processor per Bedrock should enable the memory uncorrectable bit.

struct.name: ERR_INT_MASK_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Masks the error pending bits for CPU B. A set bit lets that error raise the level 6 interrupt to CPU B. The header says only one processor per Bedrock should enable the memory uncorrectable bit.

struct.name: ERR_STACK_ADDR_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Address of the next write to the CPU A error stack. It increments after each write, and only the low bits that the stack size selects count up. The header says it is not reset by a soft reset.

struct.name: ERR_STACK_ADDR_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Address of the next write to the CPU B error stack. It increments after each write, and only the low bits that the stack size selects count up. The header says it is not reset by a soft reset.

struct.name: ERR_STACK_SIZE
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Size of the error stack that is spooled to local memory when an error occurs. The header describes it as a count of 64-bit entries and says it is not reset by a soft reset. The encoding of the four-bit field is not given in this header.

struct.name: ERR_STATUS0_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: First error status record for CPU A. Saved only when the valid bit is set. Writing the matching clear alias clears both status records for this CPU. The header says it is not reset by a soft reset.

struct.name: ERR_STATUS0_A_CLR
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Write-clear alias of the first error status record for CPU A. Any write clears both the status 0 and status 1 records for this CPU.

struct.name: ERR_STATUS1_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Second error status record for CPU A. The header says it is not reset by a soft reset.

struct.name: ERR_STATUS1_A_CLR
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Write-clear alias of the second error status record for CPU A. Any write clears both status records for this CPU.

struct.name: ERR_STATUS0_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: First error status record for CPU B. Saved only when the valid bit is set. Writing the matching clear alias clears both status records for this CPU. The header says it is not reset by a soft reset.

struct.name: ERR_STATUS0_B_CLR
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Write-clear alias of the first error status record for CPU B. Any write clears both the status 0 and status 1 records for this CPU.

struct.name: ERR_STATUS1_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Second error status record for CPU B. The header says it is not reset by a soft reset.

struct.name: ERR_STATUS1_B_CLR
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Write-clear alias of the second error status record for CPU B. Any write clears both status records for this CPU.

struct.name: SPOOL_CMP_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Spool compare for CPU A. The header gives the field only.

struct.name: SPOOL_CMP_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Spool compare for CPU B. The header gives the field only.

struct.name: CRB_TIMEOUT_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Coherency request buffer timeout. The header says a timeout can be forced by writing one bits; the two fields are named read and write.

struct.name: CRB_TIMEOUT_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Coherency request buffer timeout. The header says a timeout can be forced by writing one bits; the two fields are named read and write.

struct.name: SYSAD_ERRCHK_EN
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Controls error checking and forwarding of system bus errors. The header does not give a reset value.

struct.name: FORCE_BAD_CHECK_BIT_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: For CPU A: when reply data arrives with the uncorrectable indicator set, the check bits sent on the system bus are inverted in each set position, and the data quality indicator is not asserted.

struct.name: FORCE_BAD_CHECK_BIT_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: For CPU B: when reply data arrives with the uncorrectable indicator set, the check bits sent on the system bus are inverted in each set position, and the data quality indicator is not asserted.

struct.name: NACK_CNT_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Counts CPU A's negative acknowledgements while the count is enabled. The count clears on any other reply. When a negative acknowledgement arrives with the count equal to the compare, the count clears, the processor gets an error reply instead, and the CPU A NACK bit is set.

struct.name: NACK_CNT_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Counts CPU B's negative acknowledgements while the count is enabled. The count clears on any other reply. When a negative acknowledgement arrives with the count equal to the compare, the count clears, the processor gets an error reply instead, and the CPU B NACK bit is set.

struct.name: NACK_CMP
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Compare value for both NACK counts. It affects both processors on this interface.

struct.name: SPOOL_MASK
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Chooses which error kinds are spooled. A set bit spools that error. It affects both processors on this interface.

struct.name: SPURIOUS_HDR_0
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Captures the header of an incoming message that matches no coherency request buffer entry while the valid bit is clear. Write zero to clear. The header says it is not reset by a soft reset.

struct.name: SPURIOUS_HDR_1
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Second half of the spurious message capture. Write zero to clear. The header says it is not reset by a soft reset.

struct.name: ERR_INJECT
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Arms the injection of one error kind into the next outbound system bus transfer of that type. The bit clears when the error is injected. Writing does not cause a transaction. A bit stays set until a matching transfer occurs, so software can poll it. Data quality injection is not in this register.

struct.name: REPLY_LEVEL
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Stops the processors from issuing requests while the reply FIFO holds more entries than this value. The FIFO holds 63 entries, so a value of 63 never stops the processors, and a value of 0 stops them whenever any reply waits. The register is in its own 64 KB page.

struct.name: GFX_CREDIT_MODE
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Switches the credit counter from counting doublewords to counting transactions. The header puts it in its own 64 KB page so it can be mapped to user space. Access is not stated; read and write is assumed.

struct.name: RT_COUNTER
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Real-time counter. It wraps to zero at its maximum value and increments on each rising edge of the global clock. The header puts it in its own 64 KB page so it can be mapped to user space.

struct.name: PERF_CNTL_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Controls the two performance counters of CPU A. The header says each counter can be set to count one of several events but does not list the events. Access is not stated; read and write is assumed.

struct.name: PERF_CNTR0_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Performance counter 0 of CPU A. Forty bits wide. On overflow it wraps to zero, sets its overflow bit and sets the performance overflow bit in bank 1. Access is not stated; read and write is assumed.

struct.name: PERF_CNTR1_A
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Performance counter 1 of CPU A. Forty bits wide. On overflow it wraps to zero, sets its overflow bit and sets the performance overflow bit in bank 1. Access is not stated; read and write is assumed.

struct.name: PERF_CNTL_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Controls the two performance counters of CPU B. The header says each counter can be set to count one of several events but does not list the events. Access is not stated; read and write is assumed.

struct.name: PERF_CNTR0_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Performance counter 0 of CPU B. Forty bits wide. On overflow it wraps to zero, sets its overflow bit and sets the performance overflow bit in bank 1. Access is not stated; read and write is assumed.

struct.name: PERF_CNTR1_B
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 processor-interface register header: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Performance counter 1 of CPU B. Forty bits wide. On overflow it wraps to zero, sets its overflow bit and sets the performance overflow bit in bank 1. Access is not stated; read and write is assumed.
